summary: This file provides React hooks and utilities for integrating Bluesky social media engagement data (likes, reposts, comments) into a Docusaurus blog. It fetches engagement metrics from the Bluesky API, caches results in session storage, and resolves which Bluesky post corresponds to each blog article through URL matching or frontmatter configuration.

explanations.5: This constant limits how many people the API will return per request when fetching likers or reposters — the Bluesky API has this built-in limit.
explanations.7: This sets how long (5 minutes in milliseconds) the cached feed data stays valid before we throw it away and re-fetch from the API.
explanations.80: This type says a Bluesky embed can be either an external link card, an image gallery, or some unknown type we haven't defined yet.
explanations.99: This inner function recursively walks through nested reply threads — each reply might have its own replies, creating a tree structure.
explanations.120: This inner function records an actor's engagement (like/repost/comment) by either creating a new entry for them or adding to their existing one.
explanations.139: We sort by number of actions in descending order so people who engaged in multiple ways appear first, since they're stronger evidence of interest.
explanations.144: This strips query parameters from the URL (everything after `?`) and removes trailing slashes, so different versions of the same URL are treated identically.
explanations.153: We destructure and type-cast the cached JSON data because localStorage returns a string, and we need to verify it has the shape we expect.
explanations.157: We check if the cached timestamp is older than 5 minutes; if so, the cache has expired and we return null to force a re-fetch.
explanations.170: We silently catch and ignore errors here because some browsers (like Safari in private mode) don't allow sessionStorage, but the feature still works without caching.
explanations.223: The `.pop()!` gets the last segment of the URI path (the record key) and the `!` tells TypeScript we're certain it exists, suppressing null warnings.
explanations.247: We retrieve Bluesky config from Docusaurus's siteConfig, which is a global configuration object set up during build.
explanations.251: This custom hook tells us whether we're viewing the default language version and gives us the URL of the same article in the source language.
explanations.258: We construct the full article URL by combining the site's base URL with the permalink that Docusaurus provides, then normalize it.
explanations.261: If we're in a translated locale and the current URL starts with the translation base, we extract just the slug part and resolve it against the source language.
explanations.281: This `cancelled` flag lets us cancel pending API requests if the component unmounts or dependencies change, preventing state updates after the fact.
explanations.286: We check `!cancelled` before updating state so that if the user navigated away or the effect was re-run, we don't try to setState on an unmounted component.
explanations.297: This cleanup function runs before the next effect or on unmount, marking the previous request as cancelled so it won't update state if it finishes late.
explanations.326: We check which endpoint we called, then cast the response to the correct type and extract either the `likes` or `repostedBy` array accordingly.
explanations.371: This constructs the Bluesky record URI in the format the API expects: `at://` followed by the account handle, a post type identifier, and the record key.
explanations.381: We flatten the nested reply tree into a simple list of all the people who replied at any depth in the conversation.
explanations.392: We use `Promise.all` to fetch likers and reposters in parallel, but only if the counts are greater than zero (avoiding unnecessary API calls).
explanations.397: We use the setter function form of `setStats` to merge the new liker/reposter data with the existing state instead of overwriting everything.
